items.rationale: Sections 2.4 and 7.1.7(c) support like-for-like fittings for the failed joint. Four necessary elbows are estimated at €40 gross, in line with Case 40.
Under §§7.1.8(c) and (e), a second set of four elbows of the same size and angle needs a distinct documented use. If all four are substantiated, the comparable gross cost is €40.

Section 7.1.8(e) requires the fittings and quantities to match the documented repair; five 28 mm elbows are hard to reconcile with the short 15 mm replacement run. If all five are verified as necessary, Case 40 supports about €100 gross.
Section 7.1.8(e) excludes unsupported quantities, and five 45° elbows are not substantiated for this localized repair. If the full set were verified, five at about €21 each would cost €105 gross.
One transition fitting could be needed to reconnect the run under §7.1.7(c), although the 28 mm connection is not confirmed. Case 40 supports about €21 gross for one necessary elbow.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers fixings used in the repair. Case 40 supports €9 gross for eight screws.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.8(e) require the clamp size to match the repaired installation; no 10 mm run is documented. If needed, Case 43 supports €19 gross for four.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers reinstatement fixings, and these clamps match the billed 15 mm pipe. Four at about €5 each give €20 gross.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers necessary trade labour, and this block fits within the reported attendance. At €93 per hour gross, 6.75 hours comes to about €628, consistent with Cases 40 and 43.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers necessary helper time, and the description confirms part-time assistance. At €67 per hour gross, 5.75 hours comes to about €385.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.8(e) limit payment to the roughly one metre actually replaced, not the 6.4 m billed. Case 40 supports about €15 gross for that metre.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows one travel charge per contractor per invoice. Comparable plumbing call-outs support €76 gross.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers repair consumables not already itemized, while §7.1.8(c) bars duplication. A modest allowance is €34 gross, consistent with Case 40.
Section 7.1.8(b) excludes general processing charges billed alongside labour and materials. The €15 figure is a conditional estimate only.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers like-for-like insulation, but §7.1.8(e) limits the allowance to the documented repair length. Case 39 supports about €22 gross for one metre rather than the six billed.
Sections 7.1.8(c) and (e) bar duplicate insulation and unsupported quantities. No separate use for six mats is documented; €20 gross allows for a small distinct patch if verified.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers wire used to secure the replacement insulation. The short insulated run and the unspecified piece sizes support a modest €9 gross allowance.

Section 7.1.7(g) covers distinct necessary repair time, not duplicated labour under §7.1.8(c). The reported day and a half supports about 12 hours total, leaving roughly 5.25 hours after line 9, or €488 gross at €93 per hour.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows only the first travel charge for this contractor on this invoice, even if a return visit was needed. A comparable trip would otherwise cost about €76 gross.
Section 7.1.8(b) excludes contractor protective equipment such as gloves. No separately priced repair consumable is identified; €10 gross is conditional on a covered portion being substantiated.
Sections 5.2.1 and 7.1.7(a) cover necessary disposal of removed pipe and insulation. The small load supports €58 gross, consistent with Case 40.

Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.8(a) allow necessary cleanup of the leak-affected tiles, but the bundled coating is not shown to restore a damaged pre-loss finish. If the covered work can be separated, allow about €105 gross for localized cleaning and disinfection, not all five hours.
